chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from someone he mentioned, from 'Umar ibn al-Hasan al-'Arzami, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him say: On the Day of 'Arafah, Allah looks toward the visitors of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and says, 'Return, forgiven for you is what has passed, and no sin will be recorded against any of them for seventy days from the day they return.'

key_terms.زُوَّارِ قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: The visitors of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).
key_terms.يَوْمُ عَرَفَةَ: The Day of 'Arafah, a significant day in the Islamic calendar coinciding with the Hajj pilgrimage.

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husain's grave on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the unique intercessory power of Imam al-Husayn’s shrine, linking the Day of 'Arafah—a peak moment of divine mercy in the Hajj calendar—to the specific devotion of Ziyarah. The promise of seventy days of sin exemption reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of spiritual grace extending beyond the immediate act of pilgrimage, reinforcing the theological concept of *tawassul* through the Ahl al-Bayt.
